question: Two trains having lengths of 410 m and 390 m are running at speeds of 80 km/h and 100 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cross = 410 + 390 = 800 m

Relative speed (same direction) = 100 − 80 = 20 km/h

Speed in m/min = 20 × (1000 ÷ 60) = 1000/3 m/min

Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 800 × (3 ÷ 1000) = 2.4 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 2.4 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 410 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 390 m

Speed of first train (S₁) = 80 km/h

Speed of second train (S₂) = 100 km/h

 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 Train A (410 m)
 80 km/h →
 
 
 Train B (390 m)
 100 km/h →

 
• 
 

 

 Total Crossing Distance = 410 m + 390 m = 800 m
 
 Relative Speed = 100 − 80 = 20 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Total Distance = L₁ + L₂

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = S₂ − S₁

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 410 + 390 = 800 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 100 − 80 = 20 km/h

⇒ Convert speed to m/s: 20 × (5 ÷ 18) = 100/18 = 50/9 m/s

⇒ Time taken = 800 ÷ (50/9)

⇒ Time taken = (800 × 9) ÷ 50

⇒ Time taken = 16 × 9 = 144 seconds

⇒ Time in minutes = 144 ÷ 60 = 2.4 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 2.4 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two bodies travel in the same direction, their relative speed is calculated by taking the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). If they travel in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Train Crossing Distance

When a train completely crosses another train or platform, the total distance traveled is always the sum of both their lengths (L₁ + L₂), regardless of the direction they are moving.

Speed Conversion Rule

Multiply by 5/18 to convert km/h into m/s. Conversely, multiply by 18/5 to convert m/s into km/h.
